newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA LEV ENDS FLAT, AWAITS C.BANK SUPPORT.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA LEV ENDS FLAT, AWAITS C.BANK SUPPORT.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev ended at 350-355 per dollar, in a narrower spread than 340-360 in early trade and up from 395 at the previous close as the market awaited possible central bank decisions for lev stabilisation.

"Interbank trade was extremely cautious and in low volumes after a rise in dollar supply boosted the lev to around 350 at mid-morning where it idled throughout the day," a commercial bank dealer said.

Foreign currency supply rose as Thursday's record high for the dollar of 390-395 levs encouraged profit taking both by banks and final clients, dealers said. The lev lost 18 percent to the dollar on Thursday.
However, dollar demand was lower than on Thursday as traders tried to avoid large foreign currency exposure ahead of expected central bank steps in support of the crumbling lev.
The central bank was buying dollars at 350 levs at the end of today's trade, dealers said.
BNB officials were not available for comment.
The Bulgarian National Bank's (BNB) board adjourned its regular weekly meeting on Thursday evening and continued it on Friday but no decisison was announced by 1730 local time (1530 GMT).
A rumour swept the market late on Thursday that the foreign exchange bureaux might be closed to halt a dollar rush by panicked individuals.

Bulgarians rushed to convert lev savings in hard currency this week due to rumours that they might lose their lev deposits and treasury paper investments under a currency board system being discussed for Bulgaria.
The lev began the week at 272-275 per dollar.

Under the scheme of a currency board proposed by the International Monetary Fund levs in circulation and banks' mimimum reserves at the central bank must be exactly matched with BNB's foreign exchange reserves.
